correctness.rationale: Exact fixed-content run-composition probability mass function and a separate direct exhaustive word count agree through length 13. Reconstructing all mixed transition-cluster factorial moments up to four in rational symbolic algebra yields the stated fourth-cumulant polynomial identically after a+b=n. The Möbius substitution yields one positive cubic root by Descartes sign rule for every n>=10; endpoint factorizations and the complete finite n=4..9 table prove the sharp phase, and leading polynomial terms prove the limiting proportion. The embedded standalone exact checker was executed; finite checks corroborate the universal algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches of published findings and accessible own claims did not show a statement or dominating evaluated sign theorem. Closest same-object published result gives only second-order transition covariances. Full-accessible primary work gives known pmfs and lower moments. The classical exact pmf does imply the fourth cumulant after a nontrivial evaluation, so the claim of originality is specifically the universal one-crossing sign theorem, sharp n=10 onset and limiting proportion; incomplete 1940 and 1957 scans remain material priority risks.
residual_risks: The well-known exact two-category runs pmf logically contains the fourth cumulant and could make a mere moment formula a routine derived fact. Acceptance relies on the separately proved one-boundary sign theorem.
Mood (1940), Wald–Wolfowitz (1940), Barton–David (1957), and older runs monographs were not all readable in full and may contain the same inequality under another parameterization.
Search noncoverage is evidence of plausible originality, not proof of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The fixed-composition Wald–Wolfowitz runs distribution is an operational nonparametric null. A complete exact finite-size and asymptotic classification of the sign of its fourth cumulant is a natural previously unstated higher-order dependence invariant; the first positive regime at sample length ten and unique imbalance boundary distinguish rare versus balanced class compositions. This is more than re-labeling a pmf, though it does not claim quantitative normal-tail bounds.
